  ensures result >= 0
  effects pure
  example abs_sum([]) == 0
  example abs_sum([1, -2, 3]) == 6
  example abs_sum([-4, -5]) == 9
{ match xs { [] => 0  [h, ..t] => abs_val(h) + abs_sum(t) } }

fn clamp_all(xs: List[Int], lo: Int, hi: Int) -> List[Int]
  requires lo <= hi
  ensures length(result) == length(xs)
  effects pure
  example clamp_all([], 0, 10) == []
  example clamp_all([-5, 5, 15], 0, 10) == [0, 5, 10]
  example clamp_all([1, 2, 3], 0, 10) == [1, 2, 3]
{ match xs { [] => []  [h, ..t] => [clamp(h, lo, hi)] ++ clamp_all(t, lo, hi) } }

  example is_palindrome([1, 2, 3]) == false
{ xs == reverse_list(xs) }

fn is_palindrome(xs: List[Int]) -> Bool
  requires true
  ensures (result == true) or (result == false)
  effects pure
  example is_palindrome([]) == true
  example is_palindrome([1]) == true
  example is_palindrome([1, 2, 1]) == true
  example is_palindrome([1, 2, 3]) == false
  example is_palindrome([1, 2, 2, 1]) == true
{

fn lcm(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
  requires a > 0 and b > 0
  ensures result > 0
  ensures result % a == 0 and result % b == 0
  effects pure
  example lcm(4, 6) == 12
  example lcm(21, 6) == 42
  example lcm(5, 5) == 5
{ a / gcd(a, b) * b }

fn lcm(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
  requires a > 0
  requires b > 0
  ensures result >= a and result >= b
  ensures (result % a) == 0 and (result % b) == 0
  effects pure
  example lcm(4, 6) == 12
  example lcm(3, 5) == 15
  example lcm(7, 7) == 7
{
  (a / gcd(a, b)) * b
}
